name: Ikusei Shuro / Employment for Nurturing Skills (育成就労)

requirements.blocker_text: This will require working in a designated labor-shortage sector aligned with the Specified Skilled Worker sector list, with the explicit goal of reaching Type i SSW skill level within a 3-year training period. The implementing framework is not yet fully operational as of this verification.

outcome.duration_length: 3-year training period, designed to bring the worker to Specified Skilled Worker Type i level

sources.title: Immigration Services Agency of Japan / Ministry of Justice — 育成就労制度 (Ikusei Shuro system), implementing legislation for the replacement of the Technical Intern Training Program

notes: GENUINE NEW CASE TYPE, same class as Portugal's skilled job-seeker visa: this program is ENACTED IN LAW (legislation passed 2024) but NOT YET FULLY OPERATIONAL — the statutory implementation date is 1 April 2027, with plan-certification applications reportedly beginning around September 2026. Marked 'draft' status to reflect this, same convention used for pt_job_seeker_skilled. MAJOR STRUCTURAL FINDING confirmed during research: this replaces the long-controversial Technical Intern Training Program (廃止 — abolished), which had drawn significant international criticism over worker exploitation and a documented 9,753 technical-intern disappearances in a single year (2023, a record high per Ministry of Justice data) — the reform is explicitly framed as a shift from the old program's nominal 'international contribution' purpose (widely acknowledged to have functioned as disguised labor migration) to an honest workforce-development-and-retention purpose. GENUINE TRANSITION MECHANICS confirmed: the two systems will COEXIST for approximately 3 years post-implementation (through roughly 2030) — workers already in the Technical Intern program continue under the OLD rules through completion, with continued exam-exempt transition to SSW Type i for those who complete Technical Intern levels 2 or 3 in a matching field; NEW entrants from April 2027 onward go through Ikusei Shuro instead, and — a real, confirmed difference — do NOT get the exam-exemption privilege that legacy Technical Intern completers retain during the transition window, meaning Ikusei Shuro graduates must pass both a skills test and a Japanese test (JLPT A2-equivalent or higher) to move to SSW, unlike some Technical Intern completers. This is a genuinely significant, dated, confirmed structural reform — one of the most substantial route replacements found across this entire multi-country dataset, comparable in scale to the UK's Health & Care Worker closure or Spain's Golden Visa abolition, but distinguished by its long lead-time and multi-year coexistence period rather than a hard cutover date.
